It's fixed. `split_cents(100, 3)` now returns `[33, 33, 34]`, so the shares always add up to the full total. The leftover grosze go to the last people in the list.

I also had to change `receipt.py`, which you didn't ask about. `receipt_lines` had been working around the bug by adding the missing grosze to the last person's share itself. With the fix in place, that would have charged those grosze twice, so I removed the workaround. Receipts come out the same as before. That's also why I chose to give the extra grosze to the last people rather than the first.

I added a test to `test_money.py` for uneven splits. Because I'd touched `receipt.py`, I also ran `test_receipt.py` on top of the file you named. It has only two tests and finished instantly. All 6 tests in those two files pass, and I didn't run the full suite. Nothing is committed.
